elements.element: Governing law is the law of the State of New York
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the law of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction" (28.1 and 28.2)

elements.element: Governing law and forum form a permitted corresponding pair (New York law with New York County courts)
elements.evidence: 28.1 pairs "the law of the State of New York" with "courts located in New York County, New York"

elements.element: Governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the law of the State of New York" — New York is preferred-only, not a fallback jurisdiction

elements.element: Forum is the corresponding Delaware, California, or London courts
elements.evidence: "state and federal courts located in New York County, New York"

offending_extra_words: and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction
reasons: Preferred level is complete: New York governing law paired with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, so the Singapore conflict is resolved.

Minimality fails: 28.2 already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County, so re-stating the identical venue grant in 28.1 duplicates existing protection. The tighter edit is to replace only "Singapore law" with "the law of the State of New York" and strike the Singapore forum words (e.g., "...governed exclusively by the law of the State of New York."), relying on 28.2 for venue.
The official minimality gate confirms over-expansion (10 words to 24 words, ratio 2.40; changed-character ratio 0.649).

Intent is preserved: no unrelated term is disturbed, no undefined term or contradiction is introduced; the pre-existing injunctive-relief carve-out in 28.2 is untouched and is not required to be narrowed to complete the preferred pair.
